lesson: Aggressive DD brake (5/15, min_exp=0.35) on weak base signal (IndMom+Q07 gate, FMB t=1.35) destroys returns without improving risk-adjusted metrics. MDD compressed from 64.3% to 24.2% but CAGR collapsed from 8.45% to 2.77% (below risk-free). SR actually declined (0.324->0.279). Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999) IndMom works best as pure sector rotation; Novy-Marx (2013) quality gate did not rescue weak KR-market IndMom alpha. DD overlay cannot create alpha where none exists -- it only redistributes exposure. Compare DD722 variant (SR 0.325, CAGR 4.57%, MDD 37.4%) which dominates M2 by preserving more return. Key lesson: overlay aggressiveness must be calibrated to base signal strength. Weak signals need gentle overlays or none at all.
